newsitem.title: CHINA: China disinfects tainted U.S. soybeans - paper.
newsitem.headline: China disinfects tainted U.S. soybeans - paper.

text.p: Chinese authorities have used heat treatment to disinfect part of a shipment of 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans infected with a fungal disease, the official China Daily said on Friday.

The beans were processed for their oil to avoid any spread of the soybean blight that had infected the shipment, which was imported into China in March, it quoted Zhang Baosen of the State Administration of Animal and Plant Quarantine as saying.
Zhang declined to name the source of the infected beans but said they came from several U.S. states, the newspaper said.

Officials in the southwestern province of Sichuan ordered the local importer to take special measures to prevent spilling the soybeans during transportation and processing and to burn packages, soil and other materials that might be infected.

Heat treatment was ordered by local quarantine officials and importer Sichuan Jiali Cereal Corp and Oils Industries Co Ltd was barred from allowing the beans to be used as seeds or sold, the China Daily said.
It gave no further details of the infected shipment or how the rest of the infected beans had been dealt with.
